From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap + prompt capture request (DocFlow)

Hi Julia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap below and a small request to keep momentum: 

What we heard / priorities
- Primary: automated extraction of contract clauses and obligations (high precision, low false positives)
- Secondary: conversational search over historical contracts (recall + answer grounding)
- Constraints: PII redaction, strict retention controls, and bursty traffic at EOD

Our recommended next-phase approach (high level)
- Short evaluation (2 weeks): bench a 3-model shortlist against your sample prompts + edge cases
- Bench metrics: exact-match / precision for extraction tasks, grounding fidelity for search, latency @95th percentile, and per-token unit cost
- Redaction: we need prompt examples with any personally identifiable info so we can run our redaction checklist before telemetry/benching

Action items for DocFlow (can you do these by EOD Wed?):
1) Share a representative set of ~80–150 user prompts / examples (csv or spreadsheet) with an indication of which are extraction vs search vs other — use the attached sample template if helpful (sample-prompt-template.csv).
2) Mark any rows that are "sensitive" (PII / PHI / client-specific identifiers) or include example text that must be redacted before being uploaded to our test environment. If you prefer, you can upload a redacted and an unredacted set to the Drive link we provided during the call.
3) Call out extreme edge cases (short fragments, noisy OCR artifacts, legalese with nested clauses) as separate tab or column so we can prioritize those during evals.

Preliminary model recommendations (for transparency) — we'll firm these up once we see your prompts:
- Redwood-4x-medium (fp16 / quantized) — good latency/throughput balance for conversational search and retrieval-augmented responses.
- OpenLlama-13B-q4 -> candidate for higher-precision extraction tasks when quantized and run with the KV cache enabled.
- Redwood-4x-high-accuracy (larger-context variant) — for a small subset of high-stakes extraction where we prioritize correctness over cost.

I'll track this thread and loop Ben and Marissa for bench design / redaction flow. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min intake next week to walk through the template.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Nice — reviewed the CSV quickly. A few immediate observations and a proposed bench plan: 

Quick CSV notes
- Add a column for 'expected_output_format' (json schema / span start-end) — this helps automate evaluation for extraction tasks.
- Add a 'confidence_tolerance' column for cases where partial matches are acceptable.
- Edge-case tab: please separate OCR_artifacts and truncated_clauses so we can weight them during sampling.

Proposed 3-model shortlist (initial)
1) Redwood-4x-medium (balanced) — baseline for throughput and overall cost.
2) OpenLlama-13B-q4 (quantized) — precision-oriented candidate for extraction after light prompt engineering.
3) Redwood-4x-high-accuracy (larger context) — for high-stakes extraction runs that will have human review.

Benchmark harness (automation + metrics)
- Run each model against the full sample set and the edge-case subset.
- Metrics: precision@span, exact-match on clause extraction, grounding-precision for retrieval answers, latency@95, median token cost.
- Run with two configs: low-latency (batch_size=1 / kv_cache enabled) and throughput (batch_size up to 8 / dynamic batching).
- Include a log of token breakdowns (prompt vs completion) per example so we can produce per-example cost estimates for pricing discussions.

Redaction & safety
- Before we move prompts into any hosted test environment, run our redaction checklist (attached: prompt-redaction-checklist.md). We should request both the raw and redacted CSVs to confirm the checklist is sufficient.

Rollout suggestion
- Start with a small canary of 200–500 extractions (human-in-loop verification) using Redwood-4x-medium to validate false positive rates, then expand to run automated batches with the high-accuracy model only on items flagged as high-risk.

Links / artifacts
- Bench doc (internal): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/docflow-nlu-suite
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/DF-2026-0421

I'll draft a short-runbook and the bench config tomorrow morning and share. Marissa, can you own execution? Rafael, I'll coordinate the canary plan once we have the redacted set.

— Ben

Attachments: prompt-redaction-checklist.md
